question.text: A round cylinder of weight W rests inside a V-shaped groove, touching both of the groove's slanted walls. Sketch the free-body diagram for the cylinder.
conditions: cylinder rests inside a V-shaped groove
cylinder touches both slanted walls of the groove

figure.description: A V-shaped groove made of two walls slanting inward like a wedge, with a circular cylinder resting inside it and touching both slanted walls.

solution.approach: List every force that touches the cylinder: its weight, and one normal reaction from each wall of the groove.

steps.text: The cylinder has weight W. This acts at its centre, pointing straight down.
The cylinder touches two slanted walls. Each wall pushes on the cylinder with a normal reaction, perpendicular to that wall's surface at the point of contact.
Because the cylinder is circular, the line of each normal reaction passes through the cylinder's centre, so N₁, N₂ and W all act through the same point.
steps.why_this_step: A normal force on a circular surface always points along the radius, so it passes through the centre.

steps.text: The free body diagram of the cylinder shows three forces meeting at its centre: W straight down, N₁ perpendicular to the first wall pointing toward the centre, and N₂ perpendicular to the second wall pointing toward the centre. For the cylinder to be in equilibrium, N₁ + N₂ balances W.

final_answer.value: three concurrent forces act on the cylinder: weight W downward at its centre, normal reaction N₁ from wall 1 (perpendicular to wall 1, directed toward the centre), and normal reaction N₂ from wall 2 (perpendicular to wall 2, directed toward the centre)

common_mistakes.text: Drawing only one normal reaction, missing that the cylinder touches both walls of the groove.
Drawing a normal reaction that is not perpendicular to the wall it comes from.
